section.title: The ooSQLLibrary Class
section.para: An ooSQLLibrary object is an ooSQLite library that has been loaded: a shared library, written in C or C++, that contains functions and collations, and that exports the ooSQLiteSetApi function. Unlike a package, a library does not describe what it contains: the program asks for each function or collation by the name it has in the library, with getHandle, and registers the handle on a connection with the createFunction or createCollation methods of the ooSQLiteConnection class, under the name it chooses.

Libraries are loaded with the loadLibrary method of the ooSQLExtensions class, which keeps them, and the library object is obtained with its getLibrary method. A library can also be loaded with new, as an object of the program's own that the ooSQLExtensions class does not know. The ooSQLite examples include the source of the exampleLibrary library.

section.title: Method Table
section.para: The following table provides links to the documentation of the methods and attributes of the ooSQLLibrary class.

row.entry: &changed11;Loads a library as an object that the ooSQLExtensions class does not keep.
Reflects the result code of the last getHandle on the library.
Reflects the error message of the last getHandle on the library.
Returns the handle of a function or collation of the library.

section.title: &changed11;new (Class method)
section.para: Loads an ooSQLite library and returns it as a library object that the ooSQLExtensions class does not keep.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
libName [required]
The name of the shared library, or its path name, as for loadLibrary.
Returns a new ooSQLLibrary object.

The usual way to load a library is the loadLibrary method of the ooSQLExtensions class, which keeps the library under its base name, so that getLibrary returns it. A library loaded with new belongs to the program alone: getLibrary does not return it. Its getHandle method works as for any other library.
The library must export the ooSQLiteSetApi function, as for loadLibrary: a plain SQLite extension is loaded with the oosqlLoadExtension routine instead.

Raises an execution error, 98.900, if the library can not be loaded or is not an ooSQLite library. The message says which. loadLibrary, given the same library, returns false and sets the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the ooSQLExtensions class instead.
&changed11;Before ooSQLite 1.1, new did not raise an error: it returned a library object that could not be used, and getHandle crashed the interpreter.

This example loads the exampleLibrary library with new and registers one of its functions on an open connection; the ooSQLExtensions class does not know the library:
lib = .ooSQLLibrary~new('examplelibrary') say db~createFunction('half', lib~getHandle('halfFunc'), 1) say db~exec("SELECT half(5) AS h;", .true)[1]['H'] say .ooSQLExtensions~getLibrary('examplelibrary') == .nil /* Output: 0 2.5 1 */

The simpleExtension library is a plain SQLite extension, not an ooSQLite library:
signal on syntax lib = .ooSQLLibrary~new('simpleextension') say 'not reached' syntax: say condition('O')~code parse value condition('O')~message with head ': ' . say head /* Output: 98.900 Could not create an ooSQLLibrary object */

section.title: lastErrCode (Attribute)
section.para: Reflects the result code of the last getHandle on the library.

listitem.para: 0 if the last getHandle succeeded. Otherwise, the code that the operating system gave when the name could not be found in the library; it is not 0, but its value depends on the operating system.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.
The lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes are always updated together. An error in new raises a condition instead, so a library object starts with no error.
The lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes of the ooSQLExtensions class are separate: they reflect the methods of that class.
See the example of getHandle.

section.title: lastErrMsg (Attribute)
section.para: Reflects the error message of the last getHandle on the library.

listitem.para: A message that explains the lastErrCode attribute, or no error if the last getHandle succeeded. When a name is not found, the message is the one the operating system gave, and names the library and the missing function.
The Rexx programmer can not set the value of this attribute. It is set internally by the ooSQLite framework.
See the example of getHandle.

section.title: getHandle
section.para: Returns the handle of a function or collation of the library.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
name [required]
The name of the function in the library, the name of the C function, with its exact case.
Returns the handle, a Pointer object, or .nil if the library has no function with that name. In that case the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes tell what went wrong.

The handle is what the createFunction and createCollation methods of the ooSQLiteConnection class accept to register a function or a collation written in C. Whether the function in the library is a function or a collation, and how many arguments it takes, is for the program to know: the library does not say.

A name is looked up in the library the first time its handle is asked for, or when the library is loaded, if it is named in the procedures argument of loadLibrary; the library object keeps the handle from then on.

This example gets the handle of a collation of the exampleLibrary library and registers it, then asks for a name the library does not have:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadLibrary('examplelibrary') lib = .ooSQLExtensions~getLibrary('examplelibrary') handle = lib~getHandle('reverse') say handle~class~id say db~createCollation('reverse', handle) say lib~getHandle('noSuchFunction') == .nil say lib~lastErrCode \= 0 say lib~lastErrMsg~pos('noSuchFunction') > 0 /* Output: Pointer 0 1 1 1 */
